body.title: Back-flow acceptance criteria ac1..ac9 into the Story
body.summary: The Story ships with acceptanceCriteria: [], so the nine criterionId values ac1..ac9 that the LLD test-strategy acceptanceMapping is organized around are unanchored forward-declarations — the mapping cannot be audited at review or approve time. Write the nine criteria into the Story with explicit text, using the set the LLD already makes inferable: ac1 catalog keys absent from the on-disk config are filled with catalog defaults; ac2 present-and-type-valid keys are carried through untouched; ac3 present-but-type-invalid keys are repaired to the catalog default; ac4 catalog-unenumerable namespaces (models.analyze.roleTiers, models.analyze.byRepo, models.agents) survive blindly; ac5 reconcile is idempotent and writes at most once, only when changed; ac6 maintenance.update runs the reconcile after the build step and reports it additively via MaintenanceResult; ac7 daemon boot runs the reconcile unconditionally and never aborts boot on failure; ac8 the catalog is relocated into src/config with no daemon→cli import edge; ac9 read/parse/write failures abort without writing and are surfaced as structured non-fatal outcomes. Cross-reference each criterion to the tasks that discharge it. No production code is touched.
acceptanceChecks: The Story's acceptanceCriteria array contains nine entries with ids ac1..ac9, each carrying non-empty criterion text
Every criterionId referenced in the LLD test-strategy acceptanceMapping resolves to a criterion with text — no unanchored id remains
Each of ac1..ac9 is cross-referenced to at least one task id in this plan, and every task in this plan is referenced by at least one criterion
No source file outside the Story/LLD artifacts is modified by this task

tests.name: story acceptance criteria — ac1..ac9 each resolve to an entry carrying non-empty criterion text
acceptanceMapping audit — every criterionId in the LLD test strategy resolves to a Story criterion, and every plan task is referenced by at least one criterion
